newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU Court upholds 75 mln Ecu fine against Tetra Pak.
newsitem.headline: EU Court upholds 75 mln Ecu fine against Tetra Pak.

text.p: The European Court of Justice rejected on Thursday Tetra Pak's appeal against a 75 million Ecu fine, the largest fine ever imposed by the European Commission.

The Commission decided to fine Tetra Pak in July 1991 after it concluded the company violated competition rules by abusing its dominant position in the carton packaging industry. The Commission found Tetra Pak slashed prices in order to control the European market in aseptic cartons for more than a decade.
An earlier attempt by Tetra Pak to have the fine annulled was dismissed by the European Court of First Instance (CFI), the EU's lower court.

The court upheld the CFI's reasoning that the market in the relevant products must take account of the overall economic context, making it necessary to define the products which are sufficiently interchangeable with Tetra Pak's products, in terms of objective characteristics and the competitive conditions of supply and demand on the market.
Tetra Pak argued that the fine should have been lowered because the Commission applied new methods to appraise compliance with competition rules in the sector.

"Even if in some respects defining the relevant product markets and the scope of article 86 may have been a matter of some complexity, Tetra Pak could not have been unaware, given its quasi-monoply on the aseptic (packaging) markets and its leading position on the non-aseptic markets, that the practices in issue contravened the rules in the treaty," the court said in its judgment on Thursday.
In Thursday's ruling, the European Court of Justice upheld the former judgment and rejected the claim that the fine should be annulled, or reduced.
Tetra Pak International SA is registered in Switzerland, and coordinates the policy of a group of Swedish companies with a global presence.
